summary:
Round-three machine validation passed with zero errors, as did the two historical reports. Logistics JSON and Markdown agree on welcome and check-in (16:00–16:25), icebreaker (16:25–16:45), career panel (16:45–17:30), structured networking (17:30–18:15), refreshment break (18:15–18:40), and closing activity (18:40–19:00). The six blocks run continuously in brief order in local time. Occupied staffing cells match the JSON assignments for all six blocks and use V1–V6. Accessibility includes route and restroom verification with an admission hold, clear aisles and integrated seating, accommodation intake, large-print and plain-text agendas, spoken and written changes, quiet seating, flexible participation, and seated refreshment delivery. Checked contingency triggers, actions, and owners for AV or Wi-Fi failure (V6 switches to printed and spoken cues), speaker absence (V3 redistributes questions or uses facilitated peer discussion), volunteer absence (V1 or acting V3 coordinates), and stock shortages (V5 or V2 checks stock and escalates to V1 or V3).

The six unique Budget r3 purchases match the catalog, both budgets and logistics representations of current supply quantities and costs. SNACK10 is 3 × 10 for 30 servings and 4200 cents, FRUIT10 is 3 × 10 for 30 servings and 3000 cents, WATER24 is 3 × 24 for 72 drinks and 2400 cents, TAG25 is 3 × 25 for 75 tags and 1350 cents, MARKER4 is 2 × 4 for eight markers and 700 cents, and PRINT25 is 3 × 25 for 75 copies and 1950 cents. The 60 food servings, 72 drinks, and 75 tags each cover 50 students. Subtotal is 13600 cents, reserve is 16400 cents, and total is 30000 cents. Both plans list the venue, tables, chairs, projector, and Wi-Fi at no charge. Both budget eight shared markers and 50 double-sided attendee agendas plus 25 sign or backup copies. Budget calls for confirmation of double-sided and mixed-use printing before purchase. After applying usable surplus, round food and drink deficits up separately to whole FRUIT10 and WATER24 packs at 1000 and 800 cents respectively. The cumulative 13400-cent draw limit preserves the 3000-cent reserve floor and replenishment requires timely delivery. The optional one-pack substitution preserves 60 food servings and would shift 400 cents from purchases to reserve, subject to the stated dietary, labeling, and supply-table checks.

Instagram, flyer, and email each give Women in Tech: Connect & Grow, Friday, February 19, 2027, 16:00–19:00 local time, room for 50 college students, all six matching activities and times, and [Venue], [RSVP link], and [Accessibility contact]. The flyer and email use [Speaker names]. Instagram names no speakers. Participation options, agenda formats, and the flyer and email's one-food and one-drink offer are supported. The step-free claim needs a verification condition in all three pieces. Budget r3 correctly links back to the Logistics r3 supply and opening-desk sections. Logistics r3 still links to Budget r2 for shortage operations and addresses its Marketing handoff to revision 2, whose carried-forward schedule and participation details match revision 3. Substantive round-one changes were verified. The unresolved findings prevent final approval.

findings.evidence: The Budget handoff in outputs/demo-02/logistics-r2/logistics.md named Budget revision 1. The Budget handoff in outputs/demo-02/logistics-r3/logistics.md now says Budget r2 and its actual link, ../budget-r2/budget.md#refreshment-shortage-procedure, resolves to the existing r2 shortage section. That section covers V2-to-V3 escalation and V3's replenishment authority but only provides the older pre-opening overlap instruction, with no mid-welcome acceptance protocol or speaker transition fallback. The Review note in outputs/demo-02/budget-r3/budget.md identifies the stale link. Budget r3 steps 1–3 agree with Logistics r3 on current desk coverage, V2's immediate item-level report to V3 when both leads are absent, and V3's authority to authorize timely whole-pack replenishment within the reserve limit.
findings.impact: Volunteers following the operational link can miss the accepted desk transfer and speaker fallback during an overlapping absence while handling a shortage.
findings.request: Update the Logistics Budget handoff label and target to ../budget-r3/budget.md#refreshment-shortage-procedure. Preserve the explicit V2-to-V3 escalation and replenishment authority and verify the link opens the r3 procedure with the current opening coverage.

findings.evidence: The accessibility paragraph in each section of outputs/demo-02/marketing-r3/marketing.md says the route from arrival to seating, refreshments, and the restroom is step-free. The venue remains [Venue]. Setup and accessibility in outputs/demo-02/logistics-r3/logistics.md assigns V4 to verify the full route before doors open and arrange a verified alternative if needed. V1 or acting V3 holds admission until an accessible route is available.
findings.impact: Attendees who depend on step-free access can make plans based on a route that still requires confirmation or may change.
findings.request: In all three pieces, describe step-free access as planned and say where verified route information will be shared. Retain [Accessibility contact] for advance questions and reserve a confirmed route claim for after verification.

findings.evidence: In outputs/demo-02/logistics-r3/logistics.md, the welcome staffing row assigns V2 tags and the desk at 16:22, and Setup and accessibility assigns V2 written schedule updates. The volunteer-absence contingency for V2 only folds questions into the panel and switches to one refreshment station. The separate opening-desk handoff applies when V5 is absent.
findings.impact: If V2 is absent, arrivals can lose staffed check-in when V1 starts the welcome, and attendees who rely on written updates may miss schedule changes.
findings.request: Assign an explicit backup for tags, agendas, and desk coverage at 16:22 when V2 is absent. Assign an owner for written schedule updates and specify how the desk backup takes over while V4 continues access coverage.

verified.evidence: The absence row in outputs/demo-02/logistics-r1/logistics.md moved V2 to a combined station only during the break, and the shortage bullet in outputs/demo-02/budget-r1/budget.md relied on V5 and V1. The r2 Logistics If V5 is absent table and Budget r2 steps 1–4 added backup ownership. The current outputs/demo-02/logistics-r3/logistics.md If V5 is absent table and outputs/demo-02/budget-r3/budget.md steps 1–4 preserve it. V2 counts and stages first servings and surplus before opening, verifies tally and stages at the next applicable pause after a departure, and labels food and verifies drink labels before V6 releases attendees. If V5 leaves during service, V6 pauses the queue, V2 consolidates, reconciles distributed servings against usable stock, stages the remainder and rechecks both labels, then clears V6 to resume. V2 tracks first servings at the combined station and V4 continues seated delivery. The current shortage procedure covers both pre-service and in-service deficits, usable surplus and recount, holding seconds, prioritizing outstanding first servings including seated requests, and immediate item-level escalation to V1 or acting V3. Replacement stock receives both label checks before serving.

The Volunteer assignments and absence row in outputs/demo-02/logistics-r1/logistics.md gave V1 check-in, welcome, icebreaker, and closing duties but transferred only absence coordination and cues to V3. The r2 If V1 is absent table allocated public-facing duties by block. The current outputs/demo-02/logistics-r3/logistics.md If V1 is absent table and opening handoff preserve and extend those assignments. V3 makes the admission decision after V4's route check, V2 owns check-in throughout welcome unless V6 accepts, and V3 receives speakers, welcomes attendees at 16:22 and cues the icebreaker. V3 leads and wraps the icebreaker, with V6 staging speakers or V2 taking over when V6 is on the desk. V3 announces and times the panel while moderating, with V6 on AV and networking instructions when available. V6 calls and staggers networking transitions. V3 announces the serving rule, owns replenishment and the 18:35 cue, then leads closing reflection, sharing, recap, and dismissal. Mid-event transfer starts in the current block, with V3 giving an imminent cue if the backup is unavailable. Budget r3 step 3 confirms V3's replenishment authority.

In outputs/demo-02/logistics-r2/logistics.md, the combined-absence paragraph covered stock work already underway at opening, while the V5 departure row let V2 step away during welcome without an accepted desk transfer. The Opening desk handoff in outputs/demo-02/logistics-r3/logistics.md and linked step 1 in outputs/demo-02/budget-r3/budget.md cover both absences known before opening with V6 confirming to V3 and staffing first arrivals unless V2 confirms readiness to open. If V1 is already absent when V5 leaves, before or after 16:22 V2 stays until V6 accepts in person. If V5 is absent first, V6 is stationed beside the desk during stock work and takes ownership immediately if V1 leaves before 16:22, or continues if V6 already accepted at 16:22. If V2 has the desk when V1 leaves, V2 stays until V6 accepts. While V1 remains on duty, V1 keeps the desk until V2 or V6 accepts at 16:22. On return after stock work and any immediate deficit report, V2 takes a briefing and explicitly accepts before V6 leaves, or resumes tag support until 16:22 if V1 still owns the desk. The desk owner handles check-in, agendas and tags, V6 gives seat directions from the desk when covering, and V4 stays on access. V3 gives the 16:22 welcome when acting lead. If V6 still owns the desk at 16:38 and V1 is absent, V6 signals V2 and V3 and stays with arrivals. V2 pauses stock work, briefs and stages speakers by 16:42 while V3 wraps the icebreaker, then finishes stock work and accepts the desk. V3 starts the 16:45 panel in discussion format if V6 is still covering arrivals.
